Subject: High rate of 504s from Cassini5b during morning batch

- req_20280403_1320

Subject: Re: High rate of 504s from Cassini5b during morning batch

Jonas / Marissa — triage update below.

What we observed (initial):
- Start time: ~08:45 PDT; spike lasted ~75 minutes with peak between 08:55-09:20.
- Symptom: Request queue depth for Cassini5b increased ~6x; 504s originated from request timeouts at the frontend proxy when queue wait exceeded 30s.
- Root trigger: Rapid increase in average context window for the batch workload (avg ctx up from 1.2k tokens to 6-7k tokens) combined with a small subset of long-running generation requests. This caused KV cache eviction activity to increase dramatically and IO stalls inside the runtime scheduling path.

Key internal metrics:
- KV cache eviction rate: +12x at peak.
- 99th-token-latency (model runtime): increased from ~220ms -> ~1.2s per token for affected hosts.
- Autoscaler lag: scale-up decisions were delayed because the scheduler underestimated concurrent memory pressure; we observed a backpressure cascade.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:10-09:35):
- Enabled temporary backpressure threshold per-API-key to limit concurrent queued requests (reduces tail-growth).
- Pushed a hotfix to the batching scheduler to prefer smaller batch windows when context length > 3k tokens (rollout to 30% of Cassini pods).
- Added a guard to reduce aggressive KV-eviction under transient memory pressure.

Customer-facing commitments:
- We expect queue depth and 504s to be materially reduced within 30 minutes of the scheduler hotfix roll-forward.
- Full stabilization target: 3 hours for fleet-wide rollout and tuning.

Attachments: grafana-queue-screenshot-09-20.png, kvcache-eviction-stats.csv

I'll continue to monitor; will post another update at 10:15 PDT or sooner if we reach stabilization.

— Dylan Brooks

Subject: Cassini5b update and next steps (customer-facing)

Hi Sofia — following up with a clearer customer-facing summary and immediate commitments.

First, I'm sorry for the impact this morning — we know predictable latency is critical for your pipeline and appreciate your patience. Brief summary of what we saw and actions: 

1) What happened: A sudden shift in your batch workload's context length triggered a cascade in Cassini5b's runtime (higher KV cache churn + longer per-token processing), causing queued requests to accumulate and hit frontend timeouts (504s).

2) What we did: Our ops team deployed a scheduler hotfix that reduces batch aggregation for long contexts and introduced temporary per-key backpressure limits. Those changes have been rolled to 30% and are being expanded.

3) Immediate impact: We have seen 75% reduction in 504 rate on the canary pool and overall queue depth trending down.

4) What we will do next (commitments):
- Complete fleet-wide rollout of the scheduler fix within 3 hours (ETA: 14:00 PDT).
- Run a targeted tuning pass on KV cache thresholds and autoscaler signals to prevent recurrence (ETA: 24 hours).
- Provide a follow-up RCA with timeline, root cause analysis, and mitigations within 48 hours.
- Propose a short-term credit for the affected window; Ben will propose the credit amount and follow up on procurement.

If you prefer a scheduled post-incident sync (15–30 minutes) to review impact and compensatory options, we can set that up this afternoon.

Again — apologies and thank you for flagging quickly.

Best,

Subject: Post-incident update: Cassini5b queued-timeout incident — stabilization confirmed

Hi Sofia / Nova team — quick final update for the thread.

Status: Stabilized. Our fleet-wide rollout of the scheduler change completed at ~13:55 PDT and queue depth returned to typical baselines by ~14:20 PDT. The 504s for Cassini5b are no longer observed in your traffic. We've attached the final log slice and a short timeline.

Root cause (summary): The production workload shift to longer contexts increased KV cache churn and exposed a scheduling edge case where batch windows grew inappropriately large for a subset of hosts, amplifying memory pressure and delaying scale decisions.

Follow-ups we are committing to: 
- RCA report (detailed timeline, graphs, root cause and mitigation plan) by EOD 2028-04-05.
- A config knob in the Console to opt into "context-aware batching" for your workspace (ETA: 2 weeks) so you can control behavior for long-context workloads.
- One-time service credit for the impacted window; Ben will send details to your procurement contact separately.

Thanks for working with us through the triage. If you'd like a quick debrief call tomorrow to review the RCA, we're available — proposed times: 10:00 or 15:00 PDT.
